brief.situation: 11:40 in the emergency department. You are the nurse in a monitored room. Mr. Adeyemi, 58, has kidney failure on hemodialysis and missed his last two sessions. His legs feel weak and he feels sick.
handover: Triage: ESI 2. Heart rate 64, blood pressure 156/90, SpO2 97%. A fistula in the left arm with a good thrill.

The department's policy for suspected high potassium: continuous cardiac monitoring, IV access (never in the fistula arm), a 12-lead ECG and a point-of-care potassium, and the physician called at once for any ECG change, for the ordered IV calcium and urgent dialysis.
The physician has seen him and is in the next room.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and treat as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mr. Adeyemi's QRS is widening and his rate is falling. What is happening, and what do you do?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: Missed dialysis, a high potassium and ECG changes progressing from peaked T waves to a wide QRS and bradycardia are severe hyperkalemia heading toward a sine wave and arrest.
parts.modelAnswer: He's severely hyperkalemic from missed dialysis, and the ECG has gone from peaked T waves to a wide QRS and a slowing rate. That's the road to a sine wave and arrest.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Physician now for the ordered IV calcium (protects the heart), shifting treatment and urgent dialysis; stays on the monitor with pads on; no fistula arm.
parts.modelAnswer: Get the physician now for the ordered IV calcium and urgent dialysis, keep him on the monitor with pads on, and keep the fistula arm free.

noProgress.rationale: Severe hyperkalemia with ECG changes still untreated an hour on is harm here.

scoring.modelReasoning: A dialysis patient who missed sessions with weak legs has hyperkalemia until proven otherwise. He goes on continuous monitoring with access away from the fistula, pads on, and a 12-lead ECG. Peaked T waves turning into a wide QRS and a slowing rate are progression toward a sine wave: the physician gives the ordered IV calcium now and urgent dialysis follows.

caQ.ask: While the team takes over: what does IV calcium do in hyperkalemia?

choices.label: Protects the heart within minutes, for 30-60 minutes; it doesn't lower potassium

caQ.explain: IV calcium is effective within 3 minutes and lasts only 30-60 minutes; potassium must still be shifted and removed.
